contract.rationale: Core behaviour: identical results for every valid input.
Observed return types: ['list']. e.g. list vs tuple, int vs float (/ vs //) must not change.
Element order of the result is observable (including dict insertion order).
Float results must match bit-for-bit: reassociation, FMA, or vectorised sums change low bits. Relax via constraints.float_rel_tol if acceptable.
Original does not mutate inputs: an optimization must not start mutating them (in-place tricks!).
Identity of the returned object is not relied upon.
Printed output (text and order) is observable behaviour.
Original raises: explicit=none, observed=none, implicit=['IndexError/KeyError (subscript)']. Same inputs must raise the same exception TYPE.
Message text is rarely relied upon; raise to MUST if callers parse it.
Module-level state is written (caches, counters). Removing or adding it changes cross-call behaviour.
File/network/process/stdin interaction must be preserved in kind and order.
Original is deterministic: the optimized version must be too.
Python's sort is stable; equal keys must keep original relative order. Replacing with heap/selection/unstable algorithms silently breaks this.
An iterative rewrite that no longer hits RecursionError on deep inputs is an acceptable change.
